_comment: EdgeCDSS — ventilator cards. CLINICAL CONTENT IS THE OWNER'S.
Every field marked PENDING_CLINICAL_SIGNOFF is authored by A. Azelton and
by nobody else. The engine (vent_module.py) REFUSES to serve any card whose
signoff is not true, whose reviewed_by is not an authorised signer, or whose
clinical fields still carry the sentinel — so a half-authored card is
indistinguishable from an absent one and the pipeline falls through to the
behaviour it had before this module existed.
Cards go live ONE AT A TIME. Partial deployment is the normal state.
Fill a card, set reviewed_by and review_date, flip signoff to true, and that
card starts carrying traffic while the rest stay dark.
`applies_when` is DISPATCH VOCABULARY, not clinical content: it is the list
of words that route a query to this card, and it is pre-filled from the card
names in the build request so the routing tests have something to assert.
Review it anyway — a wrong signal here sends a real query to the wrong card.

cards.title: Lung-protective baseline

initial_settings.rate_strategy: Start RR 16-20 for minute ventilation at 6 mL/kg; titrate to pH/EtCO2, permissive hypercapnia acceptable (pH >= 7.20).
initial_settings.peep: ARDSNet low-PEEP/FiO2 ladder — start 5-8, climb with FiO2 need
initial_settings.fio2: start 100% if acute, down the ladder to lowest FiO2 holding SpO2 >= 94%

titrate_on: Plateau < 30 — reduce VT toward 4 mL/kg if exceeded
pH — permissive hypercapnia to >= 7.20 before increasing VT
watch_for: Plateau > 30
Driving pressure (plateau minus PEEP) > 15
Rising FiO2 requirement = worsening shunt
Breath stacking / dyssynchrony
evac_if: Plateau/driving pressure uncontrollable at protective VT
Rising pressor requirement with the respiratory failure
cards.escape_hatch: General lung-protective/ARDS-pattern card. If the driver is a specific physiology — metabolic acidosis, obstruction, TBI, chest trauma — use that card. Assumes VT on height-derived IBW, not actual weight.
cards.actual_weight_caveat: No height on file — this tidal volume came off actual body weight, which runs high. Enter a height to dose on ideal body weight; until then treat the VT as a ceiling and watch plateau pressure.
cards.tldr: 6 mL/kg IBW, plateau under 30, permissive hypercapnia to pH 7.2.
cards._authoring_note: ARDS-pattern card. It is NO LONGER the silent default: it used to also match "vent settings", "set the vent" and similar, which made it the FIRST match for almost every real vent question and shadowed all four specific cards — a DKA query reached this card, which is F-12 with the roles reversed. A settings question naming no physiology now asks which one instead of defaulting here. Own signals only.

cards.title: Metabolic acidosis — compensation preserved

initial_settings.rate_strategy: Match the patient's compensatory minute ventilation — do NOT set a normal rate. Start RR 20-30 and titrate immediately to pre-intubation EtCO2/pH. A patient breathing 35-40 spontaneously was defending their pH; setting 12-16 halves minute ventilation and the pH crashes. Match pre-tube minute ventilation if known; otherwise start high (>=24) and correct up on the first EtCO2/gas.

titrate_on: EtCO2/serial pH — keep minute ventilation matching pre-intubation compensation, correct rate up if pH falls
Plateau < 30 — if high rate drives plateau up, accept higher EtCO2 before sacrificing lung protection and escalate
watch_for: Falling pH / rising EtCO2 in the minutes after intubation = under-ventilating a compensating patient
Peri-intubation cardiac arrest — highest-risk moment in severe acidosis
Breath stacking if high rate leaves inadequate expiratory time
Plateau climbing above 30
evac_if: pH keeps falling despite matched/maximised safe minute ventilation
Cannot achieve required minute ventilation within safe plateau pressure
cards.escape_hatch: Assumes metabolic acidosis with preserved respiratory compensation (DKA, salicylate, sepsis, severe diarrhoea). Does NOT apply to respiratory/mixed acidosis or ARDS-pattern lungs — use the lung-protective card. Correcting the underlying cause is definitive; the vent only buys time.
cards.actual_weight_caveat: No height on file — this tidal volume came off actual body weight, which runs high. Enter a height to dose on ideal body weight; until then treat the VT as a ceiling and watch plateau pressure.
cards.tldr: Match their fast breathing — start RR 20-30, never a normal rate, or the pH crashes.
references: REBEL EM Simplifying Mechanical Ventilation Part 3 Severe Metabolic Acidosis 2024
Air Medical Journal VAPOX for DKA case series 2025
cards._authoring_note: THIS IS THE F-12 CARD. The eval baseline showed 0 of 4 DKA vent queries returning any settings while 4 of 4 TBI queries did. PLAN_v4.1 5.3 has been waiting on this content.

cards.title: Obstructive — asthma and COPD

initial_settings.rate_strategy: LOW rate — start RR 8-12 to allow long expiratory time and prevent breath stacking/auto-PEEP. Opposite of the metabolic-acidosis card. Accept high EtCO2; permissive hypercapnia (pH >= 7.20) beats dynamic hyperinflation. Prolong expiration — target I:E 1:4 or longer.
initial_settings.peep: low — start 0-5; extrinsic PEEP can worsen auto-PEEP, keep minimal

titrate_on: Expiratory time / auto-PEEP — lengthen expiration, drop rate, until flow returns to zero before the next breath
pH — permissive hypercapnia, treat the bronchospasm don't chase CO2 with the vent
watch_for: Breath stacking / auto-PEEP — flow doesn't return to baseline, rising plateau, hypotension
Sudden hypotension or arrest after intubation = dynamic hyperinflation — DISCONNECT the circuit and let them exhale fully then resume at a lower rate
Rising peak (bronchospasm) vs rising plateau (hyperinflation) are different problems
Barotrauma / pneumothorax risk
evac_if: Refractory hypercapnia with pH < 7.20 despite optimisation
Recurrent auto-PEEP/hyperinflation not controlled by rate reduction
cards.escape_hatch: Assumes severe obstructive physiology (status asthmaticus, severe COPD). Disconnect-to-exhale is specific to hyperinflation — if collapse is from tension pneumothorax that is a different emergency (decompression). Continue aggressive bronchodilator/steroid therapy; the vent is supportive.
cards.actual_weight_caveat: No height on file — this tidal volume came off actual body weight, which runs high. Enter a height to dose on ideal body weight; until then treat the VT as a ceiling and watch plateau pressure.
cards.tldr: Slow rate (8-12), long exhale, accept high CO2 — disconnect if they crash.
references: Deranged Physiology Ventilation strategies for status asthmaticus
LITFL permissive hypercapnia and disconnect maneuver
cards._authoring_note: Shares vocabulary with breath_stacking_auto_peep in the troubleshooting family. Troubleshooting wins when alarm language is present; check that split is what you want.

cards.title: Traumatic brain injury

initial_settings.rate_strategy: Target normocapnia — EtCO2 35-40 / PaCO2 35-45. Start RR 16-20, titrate to EtCO2. Do NOT routinely hyperventilate — prophylactic hypocapnia causes cerebral ischaemia. Brief hyperventilation to EtCO2 30-35 is a TEMPORARY rescue for impending herniation only, then return to normocapnia.
initial_settings.fio2: titrate to SpO2 >= 94% — avoid hypoxia absolutely

watch_for: Hypoxia (SpO2 < 90%) and hypotension each independently worsen TBI outcome
Maintain SBP >= 110 mmHg (adult TBI) — the single SBP target for this card, treat hypotension aggressively
Inadvertent hyperventilation (EtCO2 < 35) outside a herniation rescue
Herniation signs blown pupil posturing Cushing response
evac_if: Signs of herniation — expedite neurosurgical evacuation, brief hyperventilation bridge only
cards.escape_hatch: Assumes isolated/predominant TBI. Polytrauma with haemorrhagic shock changes priorities — resuscitate pressure first. If chest trauma coexists, cross-check the chest-trauma card. Herniation hyperventilation is a temporary bridge, not a setting.
cards.actual_weight_caveat: No height on file — this tidal volume came off actual body weight, which runs high. Enter a height to dose on ideal body weight; until then treat the VT as a ceiling and watch plateau pressure.
cards.tldr: Normocapnia (EtCO2 35-40), SpO2 >= 94%, SBP >= 110 — don't hyperventilate unless herniating.
references: Brain Trauma Foundation Guidelines for Severe TBI 4th ed
Emergency Neurological Life Support ENLS 6.0 TBI
cards._authoring_note: Control card for the F-12 regression test: TBI vent queries already answered correctly through RAG, so this card must not make them worse. S-7 also flagged three different SBP targets across three TBI answers — a card is where that gets settled.

cards.title: Chest trauma

initial_settings.rate_strategy: Start RR 16-20 for normal minute ventilation; titrate to EtCO2/pH.
initial_settings.peep: 5 — supports oxygenation of contused lung; be alert positive pressure can convert a simple pneumothorax to tension
initial_settings.fio2: titrate to SpO2 >= 94% — contusion often needs more

titrate_on: SpO2/oxygenation — contusion worsens over 24-48h FiO2/PEEP need may climb
watch_for: Positive-pressure ventilation can convert a simple pneumothorax to TENSION — sudden rising peak pressures + hypotension + unilateral absent breath sounds = decompress NOW (needle/finger) do not troubleshoot the vent first
Pulmonary contusion evolving — worsening hypoxia over hours
Rising airway pressures subcutaneous emphysema
Haemodynamic instability = tension pneumo haemothorax or cardiac/great-vessel injury
evac_if: Signs of massive haemothorax or cardiac injury
cards.escape_hatch: Assumes blunt/penetrating chest trauma being ventilated. Does NOT override the safety gate's tension-pneumothorax response — if tension physiology is present decompression comes before any ventilator adjustment. For predominant TBI or ARDS-pattern failure use those cards.
cards.actual_weight_caveat: No height on file — this tidal volume came off actual body weight, which runs high. Enter a height to dose on ideal body weight; until then treat the VT as a ceiling and watch plateau pressure.
cards.tldr: 6 mL/kg, watch for tension pneumo on positive pressure — decompress before you touch the vent.
references: Standard trauma-ventilation consensus lung-protective VT for pulmonary contusion tension-pneumothorax-on-PPV recognition
cards._authoring_note: Overlaps chest_trauma with the tension-pneumo override in the safety gate; they answer different questions and should not contradict each other.
